independence_statement: Created after reading only the pinned raw paper, before reading the candidate proposal, conceptual mirror protocol, graph, or prior review. Parent task metadata is known, but candidate wording has not been inspected.

expectations.claim: For a real symmetric precision A with I_d <= A <= kappa I_d, centered quadratic f_A(x)=1/2 x^T A x has exact first-order reply (1/2 <x,Ax>,Ax). Exact value-and-gradient, gradient-only, and matrix-vector access have the same query cost.
assumptions: A real symmetric in normalized precision class
expectations.failure_boundary: No noisy, finite-precision, nonquadratic, shifted/unknown-minimizer oracle, or approximate-reply claim.

expectations.claim: For determinant hard blocks A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I_n-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), the Ax_j reply is reconstructed from the forward O_j x_j and inverse O_j^T x_j primitive replies; append z on the identity remainder, and recover value by half the inner product.
assumptions: determinant components share b in {-1,+1} and are independent conditional on b for hardness, though the algebraic identity is pointwise
expectations.cost: One full first-order query uses at most two primitive queries per block: at most 2k overall, not two overall. T full queries use <=2T per block and <=2Tk overall.
expectations.failure_boundary: Only forward simulation is shown: FO_AO generally does not recover O_j or both primitive maps. Orthogonal-factor replies are richer than precision replies.

expectations.claim: The B.1 downstream reduction uses deterministic worst-case query caps, with at most 2T primitive queries to each block and strict 2T<n; this is the budget needed for the adaptive primitive transcript indistinguishability argument.
assumptions: T deterministic cap for every input and seed
adaptivity uses Borel functions of earlier responses and an independent input-independent seed
expectations.failure_boundary: Algebraic one-query identities do not themselves establish adaptive simulation, transcript equality, output-law equality, the B.1 theorem, or a formal finite-horizon cap. Do not conflate expected cost with per-run cap.

expectations.claim: Section 4 uses theta_i=(i-1/2)pi/d, lambda_i=(kappa+1)/2+((kappa-1)/2)cos theta_i and A=O Lambda O^T. The same O defines A_2, with A=(kappa-1)A_2-(kappa-2)I_d. A single exact reply for either matrix at x determines the other at that x.
assumptions: d>=2 and kappa>=2 for the hard-family construction
same dimension, cosine grid, and rotation O
kappa-1 nonzero for the reverse reconstruction
expectations.cost: One matrix-vector reply in either direction, with exact local affine arithmetic; first-order equivalence follows only from E1.
expectations.failure_boundary: This affine identity relates precision matrices and oracle replies, not their Gaussian sample laws. It does not transfer TV accuracy or identify the two target Gaussians.

expectations.claim: In Section 4 the spectrum is deterministic and may be supplied to the algorithm; the Gaussian normalizing constant is known. The hidden object is the random Haar eigenbasis, independent of the algorithm seed. This differs from determinant-sign hardness.
expectations.failure_boundary: Known spectrum does not supply the eigenbasis or eliminate the sampling hardness. Do not call this hidden eigenvalue or unknown normalizer hardness, and do not deduce a spectrum-known property for the determinant family.

expectations.claim: Main determinant lower bound requires d>=1, kappa>=4, 0<epsilon<=1/16. Fixed-spectrum lower bound requires fixed delta in (0,1), d>=d0(delta), 2<=kappa<=d^(1-delta), 0<epsilon<=1/10. The fixed-spectrum affine query identity is a source statement under its hard-family scope, not a proof of those lower bounds.
expectations.failure_boundary: No uniform extension of fixed-spectrum hardness to all kappa, all dimensions, or accuracy-dependent growth. Theorem proof limitations remain proof limitations, not impossibility results for the family.

expectations.claim: A source-level correspondence may organize the exact oracle factorization and its costs without claiming Lean implication, certified transport/functor, theorem equivalence, sampling-law transport, preservation of TV or automatic transfer of hardness.
expectations.failure_boundary: Formal certification and source theorem V must be assessed by a separate authorized mathematical workflow. Their status cannot be inferred from this review.

comparison_criteria: Exact source anchors and parameter scope
Critical identities including block remainder and sign/coefficient normalization
Direction and multiplicative cost of oracle simulation
Strict per-block cap versus global or expected budget
Known deterministic spectrum versus hidden eigenbasis and determinant sign
Conclusion and failure boundaries excluding sample-law/TV/formal transfer
Semantic novelty versus existing oracle-reduction and gaussian-hidden-information bridges
